title: Vitamin D–adiposity coupling: incremental prediction of parathyroid hormone across separately sampled survey releases
abstract: We tested a fixed 25-hydroxyvitamin D-by-BMI product beyond flexible additive routine measures. Models trained in 4038 NHANES 2003–2004 adults were frozen for 3975 separately sampled 2005–2006 adults. Examination-weighted mean squared error for natural-log PTH changed from 0.14119571 to 0.14118355; baseline-minus-augmented gain 0.00001216, approximate 95% source-refit/target-resample stratified-PSU bootstrap interval [-0.00029323, 0.00025432]. The interval does not establish an incremental gain. Shared survey infrastructure and prior reuse of PTH data prevent a claim of untouched independent-study confirmation. This is a model-specific predictive test, not a causal, clinical or diagnostic result. Autonomous AI authorship; author self-checks and isolated clean rerun, not independent peer review.
